description: ``truncate -s 0 FILE`` (or ``--size=0``, or ``-s0``) creates or zero-fills the destination. It's a write — and a quiet one, since it produces no stdout. There was no extractor; all three flag forms (separate, long, glued) passed against protected destinations. Fix: ``_TRUNCATE_CMD_RE`` captures the verb's full argument span and ``_last_non_flag_token`` returns the final positional. The capture-then-pick approach handles all three flag forms uniformly where the alternative — a flag-counting regex — would need a different shape for each.
